title: What BART’s 36 archived investigation reports found, 2019–2023
question: Which allegations did the inspector general substantiate, clear or leave unresolved, and what records would settle the remaining questions?
finding: The archive includes unsupported billing, contract splitting, gaps in inventory records, and allegations the inspector general cleared. Each row links the issuer’s report and identifies its conclusion.
how: Each row represents one PDF on the OIG’s 2019–2023 investigation archive. Several PDFs summarize multiple allegations. The report date, scope and wording come from the document. Later settlement and recommendation records are identified separately.
limits: A PDF can summarize several matters or provide only limited initial findings. A referral, potential penalty, spending authorization, settlement and receipt have different meanings. The row count cannot be used to estimate a rate of misconduct.

rows.subject: Force-account construction invoices
rows.outcome: The OIG reported $1.7 million of invoices without the required support. Its $8.3 million estimate concerned potential statutory damages and penalties.
rows.next: The later settlement file records $1.7 million actually recovered.

rows.subject: Seven employee-misconduct investigations
rows.outcome: The OIG reviewed seven separate allegations of time theft, vehicle misuse, conflicts or document disclosures. Some were substantiated and others were not.
rows.next: Use its separate findings and case numbers before pursuing any recovery.

rows.subject: Starting salaries and hiring documentation
rows.outcome: The OIG found allowable factors supported one starting salary and that BART had not applied the same documented factors consistently to nine others.
rows.next: Check the resulting placement decisions and monitoring; protected status alone does not establish damages.

rows.subject: Public-records disclosures
rows.outcome: BART inadvertently disclosed protected information in three responses. Investigators found no indication of a willful release.
rows.next: Check the subsequent records-review procedures without identifying the people whose information was released.

rows.subject: Promotional merchandise
rows.outcome: Distribution records did not account for 61 promotional items valued at $1,151.
rows.next: The report supports an inventory gap. Establish any actual theft or repayment from separate records.

rows.subject: Downtown San Francisco outreach agreements
rows.outcome: BART paid $350,000. The OIG confirmed outreach and one treatment admission; other outcomes were unclear. The bed-access allegation was unsubstantiated.
rows.next: The Board minutes and management response distinguish outreach, voluntary treatment and emergency beds.

rows.subject: Financial advisory work outside a prime contract
rows.outcome: The OIG found a $56,000 avoidable administration charge when $1.6 million of financial-advisory workplans were placed through an engineering prime contract.
rows.next: The FY2025 annual report marks the scope-review recommendation implemented. The individual workplans and any billing credit remain to be checked.

rows.subject: Subconsultants and disadvantaged-business development
rows.outcome: The OIG identified a missed opportunity to develop existing disadvantaged businesses when firms were added after award. It did not find the alleged technical violation of the DBE rules.
rows.next: Check approved substitutions and employees’ documented justification against later procedures.

rows.subject: Link21 expenditure reporting
rows.outcome: The OIG found that financial reporting did not give the public a clear view of Link21 spending. It distinguished contract awards from optional future work.
rows.next: Compare later public expenditure reports with paid invoices. Keep options separate from spending.

rows.subject: Financial interests in BART contracting
rows.outcome: The OIG found two former BART employees helped make contracts from which they later benefited. A third employee violated District disclosure rules. BART disqualified the bidder in that procurement and prevented a statutory financial conflict.
rows.next: BART canceled the affected workplans and contracts. It declined to seek return of $1,249,066 in payments. The FY2023 annual report records both decisions.

rows.subject: Paid time at nonwork locations
rows.outcome: The OIG found an employee spent substantial parts of claimed duty hours at home or other nonwork locations.
rows.next: Look for an agency recovery or personnel disposition in aggregate without naming employees.

rows.subject: Manager’s overtime allocation
rows.outcome: The manager’s overtime was neither unexplained nor excessive, and investigators found no evidence the manager took work from staff.
rows.next: Exclude this allegation from overtime-loss estimates.

rows.subject: Discipline for employees in the same incident
rows.outcome: The OIG found BART followed the required procedures in the disciplinary matter it reviewed. It explained how mitigating and aggravating factors can affect individual outcomes.
rows.next: The report supplies no public-funds loss.

rows.subject: Graffiti-removal safety inquiry
rows.outcome: The OIG reported that union instructions prevented it from completing its investigation into worker training and safety procedures.
rows.next: The uncompleted inquiry establishes no conclusion on the underlying safety allegation.

rows.subject: Federal faregate money and local bicycle access
rows.outcome: The OIG found the local Measure RR reallocation and $4.335 million federal faregate award were allowable. It rejected the allegation that BART improperly swapped federal funding.
rows.next: Keep the two funding decisions distinct; no disallowed grant cost was found.

rows.subject: End-of-shift timekeeping
rows.outcome: The OIG found inconsistent documentation of end-of-shift pay and identified a need to clarify when contract rules allow the time.
rows.next: Reconcile corrected entries against the operative labor agreement before estimating a loss.

rows.subject: Employee purchasing-card transactions
rows.outcome: The OIG questioned the business justification and handling of specific purchases, including a wagon and headphones.
rows.next: Check disposition or business use of the items. The report does not show that every purchase was fraudulent.

rows.subject: Workplan selection and consultants’ costs
rows.outcome: The evidence did not establish inflated overhead rates. The OIG reported that the allocation process could create the appearance of an unfair advantage.
rows.next: Use individual workplans and selection records before attributing a preferential award.

rows.subject: Timekeeping and attendance investigations
rows.outcome: The OIG separated allegations about clock corrections, attendance and altered timesheets. Evidence differed across the individual allegations.
rows.next: Retain separate case dispositions; no total loss follows from the summary.

rows.subject: Potential interest in an on-call contract
rows.outcome: The OIG found failures to disclose a potential interest. A manager helped contract with the firm employing their spouse, who received annual profit sharing. The OIG sought outside guidance on the financial conflict and possible contract consequences.
rows.next: It did not establish every alleged financial benefit. Check the later multi-case conflict report and external opinions.

rows.subject: Correction of a purchase order
rows.outcome: Investigators confirmed that the correct vendor received the payment. A back-end correction left the vendor information inconsistent across two BART systems.
rows.next: Review reconciliation and system changes before treating a vendor discrepancy as an improper payment.

rows.subject: Elected official’s social media
rows.outcome: The OIG found no evidence that a Board director’s social media use created a financial conflict. It recommended separate personal and official accounts. The Board declined the recommendation.
rows.next: The report identifies no improper payment.

rows.subject: Customs storage and duplicate delivery charges
rows.outcome: The underlying warehouse-services arrangement was properly authorized, but the OIG identified $1,410 of avoidable customs storage fees and duplicate delivery charges.
rows.next: Check the freight bills, subsequent contract terms and itemized recovery separately.

rows.subject: Technology procurement through purchasing schedules
rows.outcome: The OIG found BART mischaracterized technology purchases from Oracle and SHI as authorized under NASPO ValuePoint.
rows.next: Verify each order’s actual authority and approvals. The report distinguishes training gaps from intentional evasion.

rows.subject: Payroll consultant and Board approval
rows.outcome: Twelve agreements generated over $1.46 million in payments. The OIG substantiated contract splitting and confirmed that the consultant provided the work.
rows.next: The case includes management’s two-scope explanation and later closure of both recommendations.

rows.subject: Retired officers’ pay and benefits
rows.outcome: The OIG found slow handling of retiree wage and benefit errors. A retired officer prevailed in a wage lawsuit and BART paid the officer.
rows.next: Get the judgment, payment and agency claims reconciliation before quantifying any wider shortfall.

rows.subject: Equipment returned by retirees
rows.outcome: Managers and retirees received property-return instructions. BART received only 130 of 287 checklists and the OIG found some property had not been collected. It recommended contacting the other 157 retirees.
rows.next: Use individual return receipts and later follow-up to establish any actual loss.

rows.subject: Consultant invoice and $3,204 error
rows.outcome: A detailed invoice review found no evidence of intentional false billing. An identified $3,204 overbilling was acknowledged and the prime agreed to refund it.
rows.next: The FY2022 OIG annual report marked recovery implemented. A ledger gives any exact posting date.

rows.subject: External financial auditor selection
rows.outcome: The OIG found the Board and Audit Committee received valid scores; it found no support for the related retaliatory termination allegation.
rows.next: No improper award was established.

rows.subject: Pension reporting of special compensation
rows.outcome: The OIG examined employee communications and the limits on CalPERS special compensation reporting. One email could be misinterpreted.
rows.next: Use the rules applying to the particular benefit and period. The report gives no basis to count all such compensation as a loss.

rows.subject: Unattended storeroom access
rows.outcome: The longstanding procedure omitted later positions and the inventory system. The OIG recommended updating it.
rows.next: The procedural gap does not establish inventory theft.

rows.subject: Relatives working in the same facility
rows.outcome: The OIG found the different-shift employment arrangement did not violate BART’s employment and assignment of relatives policy.
rows.next: Keep this disposition separate from later substantiated nepotism matters.

rows.subject: Computer reseller pricing
rows.outcome: The OIG found no overcharge on standard computer purchases. Dell’s changing prices created an opportunity to obtain a lower price in one instance.
rows.next: Check contemporaneous quotations before treating a later lower quote as an overpayment.

rows.subject: Free transit passes at a bicycle event
rows.outcome: Pandemic changes reduced the free passes ordered and the volunteer capacity. The OIG explained why bags containing passes ran out.
rows.next: No diversion finding is supported by the shortage.

rows.subject: Hiring-panel scoring error
rows.outcome: A scoring correction led to the correct candidate receiving the promotion. An erroneous offer had already gone to someone else.
rows.next: Follow up on scoring checks; the OIG confirmed the corrected selection.

rows.subject: M-Line lighting fixture specifications
rows.outcome: The OIG’s revised 2019 report found that BART approved a lighting fixture that did not meet several contract specifications.
rows.next: The March 2024 follow-up reports $2.4 million paid in a termination settlement that included equipment and mobilization. The value received and replacement procurement matter to any estimate of loss.

sources.t: FY2022 annual report, consultant invoice recommendation (PDF)
